                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`/home/user/app` contains a freshly created, minimal **Wasp 0.25.0** project (dependencies already installed). Turn it into **PollRoom**: a multi-user voting app where polls are created over HTTP and voted on in real time over WebSockets, with every subscriber receiving live, personalized results.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"All poll, option and vote data must live in the app's database. Keep the project's existing SQLite datasource and its `DATABASE_URL` configuration exactly as they are, and make sure the database schema is migrated so the app starts cleanly.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### 1. Authentication\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Enable Wasp's username & password authentication with the user entity named `User`.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Wasp\'s default auth HTTP endpoints must stay available and unchanged: `POST /auth/username/signup` and `POST /auth/username/login` (accepting `{"username": string, "password": string}`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The poll page requires an authenticated user; unauthenticated visitors of that page must end up on `/login`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### 2. Data model (`schema.prisma`)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Define at least these models, with exactly these model names and field names (extra fields are allowed):\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `Poll`: `id` (Int, autoincrement, primary key), `slug` (String, unique), `question` (String), `isClosed` (Boolean, default `false`), `revision` (Int, default `0`), `creatorId` (Int, relation to `User`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `PollOption`: `id` (Int, autoincrement, primary key), `pollId` (Int, relation to `Poll`), `label` (String), `position` (Int). A poll may never contain two options with the same `position`, enforced by a database-level unique constraint over (`pollId`, `position`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `Vote`: `id` (Int, autoincrement, primary key), `pollId` (Int, relation to `Poll`), `optionId` (Int, relation to `PollOption`), `userId` (Int, relation to `User`). A user may never hold more than one vote in the same poll, enforced by a database-level unique constraint over (`pollId`, `userId`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"`revision` is the poll's mutation counter. It starts at `0` when the poll is created and increases by exactly `1` for every *accepted* mutation of that poll (a new vote, a changed vote, a retracted vote, or the poll being closed). Rejected requests and no-op requests must never change it. Concurrent accepted mutations must never lose an increment: after N accepted mutations the poll's `revision` must equal N.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### 3. HTTP API\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'#### `POST /api/polls`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Creates a poll owned by the authenticated user. The caller authenticates with the session id returned by the login endpoint, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <sessionId>`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Request body:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{ "slug": string, "question": string, "options": string[] }\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Responses:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `401` with body `{"error": "UNAUTHENTICATED"}` when the request carries no valid session.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `400` with body `{"error": "INVALID_PAYLOAD"}` when `slug` does not match `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`, or `question` is not a non-empty string, or `options` is not an array of 2 to 8 non-empty strings, or `options` contains duplicate values.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `409` with body `{"error": "SLUG_TAKEN"}` when a poll with that `slug` already exists.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `201` with body:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "slug": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "question": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "isClosed": false,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "revision": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "creator": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "options": [{ "id": number, "label": string, "position": number }]\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`creator` is the username of the authenticated caller. Options are stored in request order, receive `position` values `0, 1, 2, ...` in that order, and are returned ordered by `position` ascending.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Validation is checked in the order given above (`401`, then `400`, then `409`), and a rejected request must not create anything.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'#### `GET /api/polls/:slug/results`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Public endpoint, must work with no authentication at all.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `404` with body `{"error": "POLL_NOT_FOUND"}` when no poll has that slug.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `200` with body:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "slug": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "question": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "isClosed": boolean,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "revision": number,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "totalVotes": number,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "leaderOptionId": number | null,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "options": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'    { "id": number, "label": string, "position": number, "votes": number, "voters": string[] }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `options` is ordered by `position` ascending.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `votes` is the number of votes currently held by that option; `totalVotes` is the sum over all options.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `voters` is the list of usernames of the users currently voting for that option, sorted ascending by Unicode code point.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `leaderOptionId` is `null` when the poll has no votes; otherwise it is the `id` of the option with the most votes, ties broken in favor of the smallest `position`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### 4. WebSocket protocol\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"The app must expose Wasp's WebSocket support on the server (same origin/port as the HTTP server). All events below use a single JSON object as their only argument.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Events accepted from clients:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'| Event              | Payload                                  |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `poll:subscribe`   | `{ "slug": string }`                     |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `poll:unsubscribe` | `{ "slug": string }`                     |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `poll:vote`        | `{ "slug": string, "optionId": number }` |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `poll:retract`     | `{ "slug": string }`                     |\n'[39m +
                [32m'| `poll:close`       | `{ "slug": string }`                     |\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Events emitted by the server:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll:state`, whose payload is **personalized per receiving connection**:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "slug": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "question": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "isClosed": boolean,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "revision": number,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "totalVotes": number,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "leaderOptionId": number | null,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "myVoteOptionId": number | null,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "options": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'    { "id": number, "label": string, "position": number, "votes": number, "voters": string[] }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"All fields follow the same rules as `GET /api/polls/:slug/results`; `myVoteOptionId` is the id of the option the *receiving* connection's user currently votes for in this poll, or `null` if that user has no vote in it.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll:error`, with payload `{ "code": string, "message": string }`, where `message` is a non-empty human-readable string. It is delivered only to the connection that sent the offending event, and it never changes any stored state.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Behaviour:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll:subscribe` makes the connection a subscriber of that poll and replies with `poll:state` to that connection only. Subscribing again while already subscribed is allowed and behaves the same way. A connection may be subscribed to several polls at once.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* `poll:unsubscribe` removes the connection from that poll's subscribers and emits nothing back. The connection must stop receiving that poll's broadcasts.\n"[39m +
                [32m"* `poll:vote` records (or moves) the calling user's single vote in that poll onto `optionId`. If the user already votes for that exact option, the request is a no-op: `revision` must not change and `poll:state` must be sent to the requesting connection only. Otherwise the mutation is accepted.\n"[39m +
                [32m"* `poll:retract` removes the calling user's vote from that poll.\n"[39m +
                [32m"* `poll:close` marks the poll closed. Only the poll's creator may close it. A closed poll accepts no further votes or retractions, but stays readable and subscribable.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Every accepted mutation (`poll:vote` that changes state, `poll:retract`, `poll:close`) must send an up-to-date, individually personalized `poll:state` to **every** connection currently subscribed to that poll, including the connection that triggered it and including several connections belonging to the same user. Connections that are not subscribed to that poll must receive nothing.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Error codes, checked in this exact precedence order for every event:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'1. `UNAUTHENTICATED` — the connection has no authenticated user.\n'[39m +
                [32m'2. `INVALID_PAYLOAD` — the payload is missing, is not an object, `slug` is not a non-empty string, or (for `poll:vote`) `optionId` is not an integer number.\n'[39m +
                [32m'3. `POLL_NOT_FOUND` — no poll exists with that slug.\n'[39m +
                [32m'4. `NOT_SUBSCRIBED` — for `poll:vote`, `poll:retract` and `poll:close`: the connection has not subscribed to that poll (`poll:subscribe` and `poll:unsubscribe` never produce this code).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Then, per event:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll:vote`: `POLL_CLOSED` when the poll is closed, then `OPTION_NOT_FOUND` when `optionId` is not an option of that poll.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll:retract`: `POLL_CLOSED` when the poll is closed, then `NO_ACTIVE_VOTE` when the user holds no vote in that poll.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* `poll:close`: `NOT_POLL_CREATOR` when the caller is not the poll's creator, then `ALREADY_CLOSED` when the poll is already closed.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### 5. Poll page (client)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'A page mounted at the route path `/poll/:slug`, requiring authentication, that renders live poll results using the WebSocket protocol above and updates itself without a page reload whenever anybody else votes, retracts or closes the poll.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'For an existing poll the page must render these elements, identified by their `data-testid` attribute:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"* `poll-question`: the poll's question text.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* `poll-status`: exactly `open` or `closed`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll-revision`: the current `revision`, digits only.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll-total-votes`: the current `totalVotes`, digits only.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll-leader`: the current `leaderOptionId`, digits only, or exactly `none` when there is none.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `poll-my-vote`: the id of the option the logged-in user currently votes for, digits only, or exactly `none`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* For every option, in `position` ascending document order: `option-label-<optionId>` (its label), `option-votes-<optionId>` (its vote count, digits only), `option-voters-<optionId>` (its voters' usernames joined with `,` and no spaces, in the same order as the protocol defines, or an empty string when nobody voted for it), and a clickable element `option-vote-<optionId>` that casts the logged-in user's vote for that option.\n"[39m +
                [32m"* A clickable element `poll-retract` that retracts the logged-in user's vote in this poll.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'For a slug that has no poll, the page must render an element with `data-testid` `poll-missing` and none of the elements listed above.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### 6. Login page (client)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'A page mounted at the route path `/login` containing a username field with `data-testid` `login-username`, a password field with `data-testid` `'[39m... 1183 more characters

                    [32m'     * @example\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```ts\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * export default async function mySetupFunction(): Promise<void> {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   // Run some code\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    setupFn?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * If you need to serve the client from a subdirectory, you can use the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * `baseDir` option.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * If you set `baseDir` to `/my-app` for example, that will make Wasp set the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * `basename` prop of the `Router` to `/my-app`. It will also set the `base`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * option of the Vite config to `/my-app`.\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     * the router will work correctly, and all the assets will be served from\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * `https://example.com/my-app`.\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     * Check the [Base directory\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     * with `REACT_APP_`. Define the schema with `defineEnvValidationSchema`\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'// PRIVATE API (sdk)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export function setSessionId(sessionId: string): void {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    | string\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    | undefined\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  return sessionId ?? null\n'[39m +

                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +

                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Automatically prepends the API base URL, adds authentication headers,\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * and handles session invalidation on 401 responses. Non-2xx responses\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * cause ky to throw an `HTTPError`; pass it through `handleApiError` to\n'[39m +
                    [32m" * get a `WaspHttpError` carrying the server's status code, message, and\n"[39m +
                    [32m' * response body.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export const api = ky.extend({\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  prefix: config.apiUrl,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  hooks: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    beforeRequest: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ({ request }) => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        const sessionId = getSessionId()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        if (sessionId !== null) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"          request.headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${sessionId}`)\n"[39m +
                    [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    ],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    afterResponse: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ({ request, response }) => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        if (response.status === 401) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // Before clearing the session ID from local storage due to a 401 error,\n'[39m +
                    [32m"          // compare the session ID stored in the *failed request's* headers\n"[39m +
                    [32m'          // with the *current* session ID in local storage.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // Only clear the local session ID if the two session IDs match.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          //\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // This prevents a race condition like this:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // 1. Request A is sent with old session ID X.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // 2. User logs out and logs back in, obtaining new session ID Y.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // 3. Request A finally fails with a 401 (because ID X is invalid).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // Without the check, we would clear the *current* valid session ID Y.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          // The check ensures we only clear the session if the *request that failed*\n'[39m +
                    [32m"          // used the *same session ID that's currently stored*.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'          const failingSessionId = getSessionIdFromAuthorizationHeader(\n'[39m +
                    [32m"            request.headers.get('Authorization')\n"[39m +
                    [32m'          )\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          const currentSessionId = getSessionId()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          if (failingSessionId === currentSessionId) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            clearSessionId()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    ],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"// This makes sure that the following handler won't try to run in a non-browser\n"[39m +
                    [32m'// environment (e.g. during SSR), where `window` is not defined.\n'[39m +
                    [32m"if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  // This handler will run on other tabs (not the active one calling API functions),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // and will ensure they know about auth session ID changes.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // Ref: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/storage_event\n'[39m +
                    [32m`  // "Note: This won't work on the same page that is making the changes — it is really a way\n`[39m +
                    [32m'  // for other pages on the domain using the storage to sync any changes that are made."\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  window.addEventListener('storage', (event) => {\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    if (event.key === storage.getPrefixedKey(WASP_APP_AUTH_SESSION_ID_NAME)) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      if (!!event.newValue) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"        apiEventsEmitter.emit('sessionId.set')\n"[39m +
                    [32m'      } else {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"        apiEventsEmitter.emit('sessionId.clear')\n"[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'// PRIVATE API (sdk)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m" * Takes an error returned by the app's API (as thrown by ky), and transforms it into a more\n"[39m +
                    [32m' * standard format to be further used by the client. It is also assumed that given API\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * error has been formatted as implemented by HttpError on the server.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export function handleApiError(error: unknown): unknown {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  if (isHTTPError(error)) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // If error came from HTTP response, we capture most informative message\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // and also add .statusCode information to it.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // If error had JSON response, we assume it is of format { message, data } and\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // add that info to the error.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // TODO: We might want to use HttpError here instead of just Error, since\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    //   HttpError is also used on server to throw errors like these.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    //   That would require copying HttpError code to web-app also and using it here.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    const responseJson = error.data as { message?: string; data?: unknown } | undefined\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    const responseStatusCode = error.response.status\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return new WaspHttpError(responseStatusCode, responseJson?.message ?? error.message, responseJson)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  } else {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // If any other error, we just propagate it.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return error\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'class WaspHttpError extends Error {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  statusCode: number\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  data: unknown\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  constructor(statusCode: number, message: string, data: unknown) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    super(message)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    this.statusCode = statusCode\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    this.data = data\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'function getSessionIdFromAuthorizationHeader(header: string | null): string | null {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  const prefix = 'Bearer '\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  if (header && header.startsWith(prefix)) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return header.substring(prefix.length)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  } else {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return null\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.).             [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +
